The *Mogharājattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 542) is a verse biographical account preserved in the *Therāpadāna* collection of the Pali canon, detailing the deeds and attainments of the elder Mogharāja. The text connects directly to the well-known dialogue of Mogharāja found in the *Mogharājamāṇavapucchā* of the *Sutta Nipāta* (Snp 5.16), and shares thematic and textual material with numerous canonical and paracanonical works, including Dhammapada verse 170, the *Mogharājamāṇavapucchāniddesa* (Cnd 19), the *Kathāvatthu* (Kv 1.1), the *Mahāniddesa* (Mnd 15), the *Nettippakaraṇa* (Ne 4), and the *Peṭakopadesa* (Pe 2). Related verses and traditions are also attested across broader Buddhist literature, including the Patna Dharmapada (*Khāntivagga*), the Gāndhārī Dharmapada, the Sanskrit *Udānavarga* (UV 27 *Paśyavarga*), and Chinese translations such as T 210, T 212, and T 213.

 Significant verse parallels and formulaic blocks—particularly within the standard introductory sequence (§0.1–7.1) and stock narrative phrasing—are shared with multiple other Apadāna texts, such as the *Mahākoṭṭhikattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 539), the *Rādhattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 541), and the *Nandātherīapadāna* (Thi-Ap 25), as well as the commentaries to the *Theragāthā*, *Therīgāthā*, and *Buddhavaṃsa* [DharmaNexus]. Outside Pali, automated machine alignments identify text matches in the Chinese *Saṃyuktāgama* (T 99) and Tibetan texts such as the *Bodhisatvāvadānakalpalatā* and *Samādhirājasūtra* [DharmaNexus].
